CREDIT MEMORANDUM
Borrower   Meridian Supply Co. (prospect, wholesale)
Request    R2025-117, 15 December 2025: $20m revolver, 36 months
Prepared   5 January 2026, for the credit committee
Decision   APPROVE A SMALLER, STRUCTURED FACILITY
RECOMMENDATION
Approve a $17m committed revolving facility for 36 months in place
of the $20m requested. It replaces Meridian's $5.18m of short-term
borrowing and carries two years of working-capital growth at 2025's
pace. Drawings are limited to a borrowing base on receivables and
stock, secured first on both. Leverage is capped at 3.25x and
interest cover held at 4.00x or more, about 30% EBITDA headroom
fully drawn; distributions are limited to 35% of the previous year's
profit. Approval is conditional on the audited 2025 accounts and the
aged receivables listing.
FACILITY PROPOSED
Limit      $17,000,000, 36 months, committed, revolving
Drawings   lesser of limit and borrowing base (80% eligible
receivables, 50% eligible stock)
Price      Reference rate + 200 bps; 70 bps undrawn; 0.50%
arrangement
Security   First-ranking security over all receivables, inventory
and the collection account customers pay into; general
security over other assets.
Covenants  debt/EBITDA <= 3.25x; EBITDA/interest >= 4.00x; dividends
<= 35% of prior year's profit
FIGURES
Debt / EBITDA                  2.22x   1.16x   1.08x   1.28x   2.30x
EBITDA / interest              8.66x  11.07x  11.46x  10.14x   5.64x
Receivable days                   48      52      58      66
Free cash flow, $m              -0.4    -2.6     2.1    -0.2
Dividends / net income           16%      9%     30%     57%
THE CASE FOR LENDING
+ Leverage 1.28x and interest cover 10.14x in 2025, at the safe end
of Fernhill's wholesale clients; fully drawn, 2.30x and 5.64x.
+ Profitable in every year; revenue up 2.08 times since 2022 with a
steady gross margin.
+ The request matches the need: working capital that has grown with
sales, funded by a facility that revolves.
RISKS, AND WHAT THE STRUCTURE DOES
- Receivable days rose from 48 to 66; the cause is not yet known.
> Overdue and concentrated invoices are ineligible and certified
monthly; the aged listing is a condition.
- Free cash flow was negative in three of four years.
> The limit is sized to need, $17m, not to the request; any
increase returns to committee.
- 57% of 2025's profit was paid out while debt rose.
> Distributions capped; the 2026 allowance is $2.21m against
$3.60m paid in 2025.
- The 2025 figures are unaudited.
> Audited accounts are a condition of first drawing.
- Revolvers are drawn hardest as borrowers weaken: Fernhill's were
90% drawn at default.
> The base falls as receivables age, before an annual covenant
test could see it.
CONDITIONS BEFORE FIRST DRAWING
1. audited 2025 accounts, not materially worse than the management
accounts
2. aged receivables at 31 December 2025 with ineligibles at or below
3. short-term borrowing repaid and its security released
4. intercreditor agreement signed
STILL TO BE ANSWERED
? Why receivable days rose, and which customers owe the oldest
balances.
? Dividends planned for 2026 and 2027.
? Whether suppliers have shortened Meridian's terms.
? Who the term lender is, and its schedule and security.
RATING
Internal grade to be assigned under the commercial rating model
before committee. Until then the loss cost uses Fernhill's book
averages: about $105k a year against $214k to $346k of margin and
fees.
